public_rationale: OpenAI announced temporary Codex availability for ChatGPT Free and Go users on February 2, 2026 [e1]. Anthropic offered doubled off-peak Claude usage from March 13–27, 2026, excluding Enterprise accounts, according to TechRadar [e2]. These records establish promotions, but do not document the claimed API credits and free weeks near June 23, 2026 [e1] [e2]. Neither record connects the offers to an effort to appear essential to investors, leaving the causal claim unresolved [e1] [e2].
limitations: The OpenAI announcement gives no end date and does not establish availability on June 23, 2026 [e1].
The documented Anthropic offer ended March 27, 2026. It provided extra usage allowances, not documented API credits or a free paid-plan trial [e2].
The records do not establish how similar the competing products were or establish or refute the alleged investor-facing purpose [e1] [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic are competing to make much the same product by giving away API credits and free weeks of access, to create the aura of an 'essential' product and keep convincing VCs and public markets that they are building the future, when they are effectively paying customers to use their products.

statement.excerpt: Both companies are now jousting to make much the same product by giving away API credits and free weeks of access to create the symbolic aura of an “essential” product to continue convincing VCs and the public markets that they’re “building the future” rather than effectively paying their customers to use their products.

from_speaker: giving away API credits and free weeks of access
to create the symbolic aura of an “essential” product
continue convincing VCs and the public markets
our_interpretation: Both companies means OpenAI and Anthropic; the immediately preceding discussion identifies their competing coding products.
The observation concerns promotional activity leading up to June 23, 2026. Earlier promotions establish a practice but do not automatically establish an offer remained active that day.
Effectively paying customers is read as subsidizing access, not necessarily making cash payments.
The alleged investor-facing purpose is a substantive causal component. Establishing promotions alone does not establish that purpose.
criteria.support_condition: Dated records establish promotional credits or free access for both competing offerings, and reliable evidence connects those promotions to the claimed effort to manufacture apparent indispensability for investors.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records refute a material promotional assertion or establish that the alleged causal account is false. A company's stated alternative purpose alone is insufficient.

Internal records, attributable testimony or a credible investigation would also need to establish or refute the alleged investor-facing purpose.
